rrn.hint: Unique number used to look up a transaction for disputes and reconciliation.

stan.hint: Increasing number that pairs each answer with its question.

mti.hint: Four digits saying whether a message is a request, answer, reversal or network message.

rc.hint: 00 means approved; other codes explain the decline.

lab.title: Message lab
lab.subtitle: Take an ISO 8583 message apart: click any segment, bitmap cell or row to see what it means.

raw.label: Raw message
raw.heading: Raw message, exactly as sent on the wire
raw.noteEasy: Each coloured block is one part of the message. The card number is masked for security.
raw.noteExpert: ASCII packager (iso87ascii) · binary fields shown as hex · PAN masked for the lab · {count} fields in total

bitmap.label: Bitmap
bitmap.heading: Bitmap grid
bitmap.noteSecondary: Each row is one byte of 8 bits. Bit 1 is on, so this message carries a secondary bitmap for fields 65 to 128.
bitmap.notePrimary: Each row is one byte of 8 bits. A coloured cell is a bit that is on: the field with that number is in the message.

detail.label: Details
detail.mtiWhy: The first four digits say what kind of message this is. The receiver reads them first to know how to read the rest.
detail.bitmapWhy: Each bit stands for one field. A bit that is on means that field is in the message, so the message never carries empty fields.
detail.absentWhy: This field is not in message {mti}. {why}
detail.unusedWhy: This field is not used by any of the lab's sample messages.
detail.unlistedWhy: The lab has no explanation for this field yet.

1.name: Secondary bitmap
1.why: On when the message uses fields 65 to 128. Another 64 bits then follow the primary bitmap.

2.name: Card number
2.why: The number printed on the card. Always masked on screen; the first 2 digits give its length.

3.name: Transaction type
3.why: Says whether this is a purchase, a withdrawal or a refund, and from which account type.

4.name: Amount
4.why: The amount in minor units, left-padded with zeros to 12 digits.

7.name: Sent at
7.why: UTC time the message was sent. It has no year, so systems must infer it.

11.name: Trace number
11.why: A rising number assigned by the sender, used to match each response to its request.

12.name: Time at the counter
12.why: Local time when the customer paid.

13.name: Date at the counter
13.why: Local date when the customer paid.

14.name: Card expiry
14.why: Year and month the card expires, used to decline expired cards.

15.name: Settlement date
15.why: The business day this transaction counts toward at cutover and reconciliation.

18.name: Merchant type
18.why: The merchant's business category, e.g. 5814 is fast food and coffee.

22.name: How the card was read
22.why: The first two digits say how the card was read (05 is chip), the last says whether a PIN could be entered.

25.name: Transaction condition
25.why: 00 means a normal transaction with customer and card present.

32.name: Acquiring bank ID
32.why: Identifies the bank that took the transaction from the merchant.

37.name: Reference number
37.why: A unique number to look up the transaction for disputes or reconciliation.

38.name: Approval code
38.why: Issued by the issuer when it approves the transaction; printed on the receipt.

39.name: Result code
39.why: 00 means approved. Other codes give the decline reason or the error.

41.name: Terminal ID
41.why: Identifies the POS terminal that sent the transaction.

42.name: Merchant ID
42.why: Identifies the merchant registered with the acquiring bank.

43.name: Merchant name and location
43.why: Merchant name, city and country code, as printed on the cardholder's statement.

49.name: Currency
49.why: ISO 4217 numeric currency code: 704 is the Vietnamese dong.

52.name: Encrypted PIN
52.why: The customer's PIN, encrypted. Nobody can read the clear PIN on the wire.

55.name: Chip data
55.why: Data generated by the card's chip, including a cryptogram against counterfeit cards.

64.name: Tamper-proof signature
64.why: A signature computed over the message. Change a single character and it no longer matches.

70.name: Network management code
70.why: 001 is sign-on, 002 is sign-off, 301 is echo.

90.name: Original transaction data
90.why: Points at the transaction to reverse: original message type, trace number, time and bank.

128.name: Tamper-proof signature
128.why: The signature sits in the last field when the message has a secondary bitmap. Change a single character and it no longer matches.

network.title: Network operations
network.subtitle: Watch the links between the two banks, the resend queue and stand-in mode when something breaks.

known.linkUp: Link to the issuing bank is up
known.linkDown: Link to the issuing bank is down, reconnecting
known.signedOnAgain: Signed on again: the issuing bank had signed the link off
known.stillSignedOff: The issuing bank still holds the link signed off
known.lateResponse: A response arrived too late for a transaction

CLOSED.easy: All normal: transactions go straight to the issuing bank for a decision.
CLOSED.tech: CLOSED: every request goes to the issuer. Opens after 3 consecutive echo timeouts or an error rate > 50%.

OPEN.easy: The issuing bank is not answering, so the system stopped sending to it. Small transactions are approved on its behalf and reported once it is back.
OPEN.tech: OPEN: nothing goes to the issuer; the switch authorizes by STIP rules and queues advices in SAF. Moves to HALF_OPEN after 30 s.

HALF_OPEN.easy: The system is sending a few test transactions to the issuing bank. If they succeed, everything goes back to normal.
HALF_OPEN.tech: HALF_OPEN: a few trial requests go to the issuer. Success closes the circuit, failure opens it again.

unavailable.easy: The switch has not reported its state. Transactions go straight from the gateway to the issuing bank.
unavailable.tech: GET /v1/network/switch is not on the gateway yet (MCN-802). No circuit breaker or STIP.

saf.emptyEasy: Nothing waiting. Every notice has arrived.

pos.subtitle: Pick a card, enter an amount and pay as you would at the counter. Or pick a ready-made scenario to see how the system handles it.

reading.rrnHint: The RRN of the pre-auth to complete

desc.rc54: The card's expiry date has passed. The customer needs another card.
desc.rc61: The amount is over the card's per-transaction limit. The customer needs to pay a smaller amount.
desc.rc62: The cardholder or the bank has blocked this card. The customer should contact the bank.
desc.rc91: The link to the issuer is down, so the transaction was not sent. The customer was not charged.
desc.declined: The issuer did not accept this transaction. The customer was not charged.
desc.reversalPending: The issuer did not answer in time. The system is sending a reversal so the customer is not charged.
desc.reversed: The issuer did not answer in time. The system sent a reversal so the customer is not charged.
desc.invalidAmount: Enter an amount above 0 and try again.

why.approved: {type, select, REFUND {The card is valid.} BALANCE {The card is valid.} other {The card is valid and the account has enough funds.}}
why.rc51: The available balance is not enough.
why.rc54: The expiry date is before today.
why.rc61: The amount is above the per-transaction limit.
why.declined: The request does not meet the card's conditions (code {rc}).

step.linkCheckDesc: The link to the issuer is down, so the request is not sent.

Money moves only on completion.} COMPLETION {The POS prints a receipt for the held amount.} REFUND {The POS prints a refund slip.} BALANCE {The POS shows the balance.} other {The POS prints a receipt; the customer gets the goods.}}
step.returnBadDesc: The POS tells the customer; nothing is charged.
step.reversedDesc: The reversal was sent and confirmed. The customer's money is safe.
step.reversalQueuedDesc: The reversal is stored and retried until the issuer confirms it.
step.amountCheckDesc: The amount is 0, so nothing is sent.

logPan.easy: Never write down or show a customer's full card number.
logPan.expert: Never log or persist the full PAN.

logKey.easy: Never write down a secret key in plain text.
logKey.expert: Never log or persist clear key material.

persistPinBlock.expert: Never persist a clear PIN block.

chaos.heading: Chaos lab
chaos.subtitle: Switch on a failure, run test transactions and watch how the system keeps customers' money safe.

count.active: {count, plural, one {# failure on} other {# failures on}}

error.toggle: Could not change the failure. Try again.
error.run: Could not start the test run. Try again.

money.heading: Money check
money.note: Whatever fails, the money in customer accounts must always equal the sum of the transactions that really succeeded.

reaction.heading: How the system is reacting
reaction.calm: Everything is normal. Turn on a failure on the left to see how the system reacts.

SLOW_NETWORK.title: Slow network
SLOW_NETWORK.desc: Every request is delayed by about 3 seconds on the line.
SLOW_NETWORK.react: Response time rises to about 3.2 seconds but stays within the timeout, so transactions still succeed.

CONNECTION_CUT.title: Connection lost
CONNECTION_CUT.desc: The line to the issuing bank is cut suddenly.
CONNECTION_CUT.react: The system reconnects on its own. Cancellations it could not send wait in a queue and go out when the line is back.

DROP_RESPONSE.title: Lost answer
DROP_RESPONSE.desc: The request arrives, but the answer gets lost on the way back.
DROP_RESPONSE.react: After 30 seconds without an answer, the system sends a cancellation. The bank refunds the money if it was taken.

DUPLICATE_REQUEST.title: Sent twice
DUPLICATE_REQUEST.desc: The same transaction is sent twice because of a network fault.
DUPLICATE_REQUEST.react: The issuing bank spots the duplicate and returns the earlier result, without taking money twice.

ISSUER_DOWN.title: Issuing bank down
ISSUER_DOWN.desc: The issuing bank's core system stops working.
ISSUER_DOWN.react: Stand-in approval takes over: small transactions are still approved and reported to the bank once it recovers.
ISSUER_DOWN.reactTech: circuit OPEN · STIP limit 500.000 ₫ · 0120/0220 into SAF

LATE_RESPONSE.title: Answer arrives late
LATE_RESPONSE.desc: The answer arrives after the waiting time has run out.
LATE_RESPONSE.react: The transaction was already cancelled, so the late answer is only logged for monitoring and moves no money.

journey.title: Transaction journey

empty.title: No transaction of this kind yet
empty.body: Make a transaction on the POS and its journey appears here.

journey.loadError: The journey could not be loaded. Try reloading the page.

POS_REQUEST.title: The POS sends the request
POS_REQUEST.easy: The customer uses card •••• {last4} at {merchant}. The POS asks to pay {amount}.

REQUEST_SENT.title: Packed and sent to the issuer
REQUEST_SENT.easy: The acquirer adds a trace number and a reference, signs the message against tampering and sends it.

LOCAL_DECLINE.title: The issuer can't be reached
LOCAL_DECLINE.easy: The link to the issuer is down, so the request was never sent. Nothing was debited.

ISSUER_APPROVED.title: The issuer approves
ISSUER_APPROVED.easy: The card is valid, the account has the funds and no limit is exceeded. The issuer debits the account, books it and returns an approval code.

NO_RESPONSE.title: No answer in time
NO_RESPONSE.easy: After 30 seconds without an answer the acquirer can't tell whether the money was taken. To protect the customer it assumes it was.

REVERSAL_QUEUED.title: Reversal saved before sending
REVERSAL_QUEUED.easy: The reversal is written to the database first, so it can never be lost, even if the server restarts.

approved.title: The POS prints the receipt
approved.easy: The customer gets the goods. The whole journey took {total}.

declined.title: The POS shows the decline
declined.easy: The POS tells the customer. Nothing was debited.

failed.title: The POS shows a failure
failed.easy: The customer is told the payment didn't go through and can try again. No money will be lost.

REVERSAL_SENT.title: Reversal sent
REVERSAL_SENT.easy: The reversal carries the original transaction's identity so the issuer finds the right one.

REVERSAL_REPEAT.title: Reversal sent again
REVERSAL_REPEAT.easy: The previous attempt wasn't confirmed, so it is sent again, marked as a repeat so it is never processed twice.

REVERSAL_CONFIRMED.title: The issuer returns the money
REVERSAL_CONFIRMED.easy: The original transaction was found and {amount} returned to the customer's account. The reversal leaves the queue.

LATE_RESPONSE.title: The old answer arrives late
LATE_RESPONSE.easy: The answer to the original request only arrives now. The transaction is already being reversed, so it is just recorded.

note.approved: The transaction completed: money was taken exactly once and the customer got the goods.
note.declined: The issuer declined, so nothing was booked: the customer's money is unchanged.
note.autoReversed: The money was only taken temporarily and then returned in full. This is why every card network needs automatic reversals.
note.cancelled: Approved and then cancelled: the money was taken once and returned in full.
note.reversing: The reversal is waiting for the issuer's confirmation and is resent until the money is returned.
note.pending: No result from the issuer yet.

countdown.ariaLabel: Waiting for the issuer to respond
